html:
Cyprus is a large island in the eastern Mediterranean, south of Turkey and west of Syria. On the map it appears as its own state from 800 to 1500, and again from 1960 to now.

Its place on the sea lanes made everyone want it. In the Middle Ages:

  • From 688 to 965 the Byzantines and the Arab caliphs shared it and its taxes, in an unusual truce.
  • Byzantium then ruled it directly until a local governor broke away in 1184.
  • In 1191 Richard the Lionheart, on his way to the Third Crusade, seized it. He soon sold it, and in 1192 it passed to Guy de Lusignan.
  • The Lusignan Kingdom of Cyprus lasted until 1489, a French speaking Catholic court ruling Greek Orthodox people, and a base for trade with the Levant.
  • Venice then held it until the Ottomans took it in 1571.

Under the Ottomans, Turkish settlers came, and the island had Greek and Turkish communities from then on. Britain took over the island's government in 1878 and made it a colony in 1925. In the 1950s a Greek Cypriot armed campaign fought for union with Greece, and Cyprus became an independent republic in 1960 under Archbishop Makarios, with power shared between the two communities.

The sharing broke down. In 1974 a coup backed by the Greek junta led Turkey to invade, and the island was split. The north is the Turkish Cypriot area, recognised only by Turkey; about 200,000 people were displaced. The Republic of Cyprus joined the European Union in 2004, still divided.
sum: Cyprus is a large island in the eastern Mediterranean, south of Turkey and west of Syria. On the map it appears as its own state from 800 to 1500, and again from 1960 to now.
